title: Notch-echo pause
idea: A solid Shelf bookmark with a pause cut out of its body. The two holes together are the bookmark's own outline, inset and cut down the middle, so the pause stands on the tail's angle and the paper under it is an even chevron.
built: The 42 dp bookmark as in s1. Two holes 8 dp wide with a 4 dp spine between them (half a hole, as tight as the app's own pause button). Paper: 11 dp at the sides, 10.5 above, and 9 dp between the holes and the notch measured square to the notch edge, so the chevron band is even along its length. The holes sit wholly above the notch's apex, and their corners take the tip radius. With 9 dp walls the paper turned into a frame, close to the outlined bookmark that means not saved in most interfaces; with 12 dp walls the holes started to look like a pair of eyes.
small: Nothing is dropped. 48 px: 28 x 34 px; holes 5 px wide, a 4 px spine and 7 px walls, the holes' bottoms 3 px lower at the outside edge (the echo). 32 px: 20 x 24 px; holes 4 px, spine 2, walls 5, a 2 px echo. 16 px: 10 x 12 px; holes, spine and walls 2 px each, with flat bottoms, since a one-pixel slant only adds grey. Glyph: 16 x 20 px; holes 4 px, spine 2, side walls 3, top 4, a 2 px echo.
risks: The most literal of the three: a pause stamped into a bookmark, the same construction as Google Play Books (a media symbol inside a bookmark-like shape) with pause in place of play. It reads as a pause sign, and as listening only to someone who knows Shelf reads aloud. The echo is quiet at 48 px and gone at 16. Two dark slots in a light shape can read as eyes; the narrow spine and the holes' height hold it to a pause.
